v1.feedback: Lucy silhouette reads instantly, palette is properly restrained (bone/amber/ember), and the ricochet scatter-return envelope is well-shaped at 3.8s. Two refinements: the tracer projectile feels gamey — consider replacing it with a subtler pressure-wave distortion that implies force without a visible bullet; and the 9s interval between strikes is metronomic — randomize it (7–14s) so the viewer forgets to expect the next one, making each hit a genuine surprise rather than a countdown.

v2.feedback: Strong piece — Lucy silhouette reads immediately, bone→amber→ember palette is exactly right, and the ricochet pressure-wave is a genuine morphological swerve that earns the 'surprise' tag. The push multiplier (5.0) may scatter particles far enough during overlapping ricochets to briefly dissolve the silhouette — consider clamping total displacement per particle to ~20% of model scale so Lucy never fully atomizes. The ground-glow plane is a nice atmospheric touch but at a=0.035 it may be invisible on most monitors; nudge to ~0.06 or drop it to save a draw call.
